title: How Businesses Work: Cost, Price, Profit
subject: money

sections.body: Businesses have COSTS: materials, wages, rent, energy. They set a PRICE for their product.
PROFIT = revenue (money from sales) − costs. If costs are bigger, the business makes a LOSS.
Price too high and fewer people buy; too low and you may not cover costs. Businesses also compete with each other.
Example: lemonade costs 0.30 per cup to make and sells for 1.00. Selling 50 cups: revenue 50, costs 15, profit 35.

quiz.q: A business sells 100 items at 5 each. Total costs are 320. What's the profit?
hints: Selling 20 cakes at 3 each = 60 revenue; with 25 costs, profit = 35.

options: When costs are greater than revenue
When revenue is greater than costs
hints: What if the answer is negative?
If a bake sale spends 40 on ingredients and earns 30, did it profit?
quiz.explain: A loss is when costs are greater than the money coming in.
